subject: Private deployment BYOK access protocol questions
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@carbonitehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: security@carbonitehealth.com
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy BYOK — clarification on operator access and handoff

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the demo last week — Carbonite's procurement and infosec teams reviewed the architecture and we have a few follow-ups specific to BYOK for the private deployment (VPC/on-prem):

- Who holds the live CMK material at runtime? We need confirmation that Redwood operators never possess plaintext CMKs or unencrypted key material.
- In a support or breakglass scenario, what is the exact approval flow, and can you provide the audit trail we would receive?
- For on-prem installations we asked about an escrow mechanism — do you offer an escrow option, or is BYOK always customer-retained only?
- What telemetry and logs will Redwood's operator agents emit from the host? We need precise retention windows and field-level redaction guarantees.
- Any operator access windows or “maintenance windows” where human intervention is allowed (and how those are authorized)?

Procurement is aligning vendor security questions to the DPA annex — if you can send a short protocol doc and an operator access matrix we can share with legal. We're on a tight cadence: security would like answers by Friday so we can get DPA redlines into our legal queue.

Thanks,
Laura Chen
Head of Security Engineering
Carbonite Health

Attachments: none (we'll attach a compliance checklist when we have your doc)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@carbonitehealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 12:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy BYOK — clarification on operator access and handoff

Hi Laura — thank you, and great questions. Quick summary up front, then attachments and a couple of technical notes below.

TL;DR:
- Customer retains control of the CMK at all times. Redwood never has access to plaintext key material.
- Breakglass requires multi-party authorization (customer SME + Redwood SRE manager) and emits a signed, tamper-evident audit record we provide in the post-incident package.
- Escrow: we offer an optional escrow workflow (encrypted, customer-wrapped) as an add-on; we do not escrow keys by default.
- Telemetry: operator agents emit health + anonymized metrics only; sensitive fields (user content, model inputs) are never included. Retention defaults are 30 days; can be contractually shortened.
- Maintenance windows: human operator interventions are limited to scheduled windows or explicit documented breakglass events; prior notification is standard except in emergency incidents.

Attached: a short protocol diagram and an operator-access matrix (stubbed filenames below) — these are designed for your legal and infosec review. If useful we can produce a narrow DPA annex draft that maps these guarantees to contractual clauses.

Technical notes (Irene is cc'd for details):
- BYOK model: we support customer-managed KMS for both cloud KMS (customer project) and on-prem HSMs. The runtime accepts only wrapped keys; Redwood does not store unwrapped keys or intermediate plaintext.
- Breakglass audit: all emergency decrypt requests create an immutable audit bundle (timestamped request, approver emails, SRE justification, and operator session recordings if session-based access was required).
- Escrow add-on: escrow snapshots are encrypted with a customer-wrapped key and stored in an escrow vault; release requires a signed request and a 3-party approval (customer legal, customer security, Redwood security ops).

Next steps: Irene can sketch the exact telemetry fields and retention controls. Priyom, I'll need procurement to confirm the add-on pricing for escrow and an SLA exception if Carbonite wants shorter telemetry retention. Laura — expect the attachments and a DPA annex stub by EOD.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachments: byok-protocol-diagram.png (figure), operator-access-matrix.xlsx (matrix)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@carbonitehealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy BYOK — clarification on operator access and handoff

Laura / team — following up with the precise technical controls you asked for, pasted below. Quoting your original ask for context.

> "Who holds the live CMK material at runtime?"
- The customer holds the CMK. For cloud-hosted KMS the CMK never leaves the customer project. For on-prem HSMs we accept wrapped key material (PKCS#11 wrapping) and store only the wrapped blob. The runtime performs unwrap operations inside the customer-controlled HSM or enclave when available; otherwise the unwrap operation requires a customer API call to the customer's KMS endpoint.

> "Breakglass: exact approval flow and audit trail?"
- Approval flow: 1) On-call customer SME opens breakglass request -> 2) Redwood SRE on-call reviews and issues a temporary session token -> 3) Customer authorizes release (token finalization). All steps are signed and recorded.
- Audit trail contents: requestor identity, approvers, start/end timestamps, ephemeral token id, reason, operator session logs, and git-sha of the runtime binary that handled the operation. We provide the exported audit bundle in JSON + signed manifest.

> "Escrow or escrowless handover?"
- Escrow is optional. Escrowed artifacts are encrypted under a customer-wrapped KEK and stored in an escrow vault run by a neutral custodian (we partner with a third party). Escrow release requires a signed, notarized request; we will include this as a contractual addendum if you opt-in.

> "Telemetry & logs — what fields, retention, redaction?"
- Telemetry category examples: agent health (cpu/mem), request latencies, queue depth, error rates.
- Explicitly excluded: model inputs/outputs, user PII, and unredacted traces of customer content.
- Logs: operator actions (who, when, what) are logged; detailed operator-session recordings are included only in audit export and kept for 90 days by default for incident investigations. Retention for logs can be set to 0/7/30/90 days contractually.

> "Operator access windows — how are they gated?"
- Scheduled maintenance: customer receives a minimum 48-hour notice for non-emergency windows.
- Emergency breakglass: as above, requires customer SME initiation + Redwood SRE concurrence. Each emergency readout increments the audit counter and triggers an automated post-incident review.

Implementation notes for your infra team: we support two deployment models for the KMS handshake:
1) Enclave-first: HSM / confidential VM does unwrap locally — recommended for highest separation.
2) API-unwrapping: Redwood will call your KMS unwrap endpoint (mutual TLS) and only receive a short-lived wrapped token — recommended for hybrid setups.

If you want, I can produce a short runbook that maps firewall/IP ranges, mTLS CA pins, and the minimal operator ACLs required for a dev canary.

--
Irene Choi
Principal Infrastructure Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: operator-access-matrix.xlsx (filled with gated roles & approval steps)

Hi Hannah / Irene — this is very helpful, thanks. A few follow-ups and next steps from our side:

- Confirmed: Carbonite will default to customer-managed KMS in our cloud project (we will share project details). For on-prem PoC we want the enclave-first option.
- Please send the DPA annex mapping the log retention options (we favor 7-day retention for operator session artifacts).
- Can you share SOC 2 Type II evidence and any third-party audit artifacts for the escrow partner?
- Procurement asks for the escrow add-on price and the DocuSign-ready DPA (we will circulate redlines).
- Timeline ask: can Redwood provision a dev canary (enclave-first) inside our VPC in the week of Oct 18 for a two-week validation window? That timing will keep our procurement and integration tracks aligned.

If you can attach the DPA draft + a short checklist for the canary network/firewall requirements we can kick the legal and infra teams off this afternoon.

Thanks again — will await the annex and the SOC2 artifacts.

Laura Chen
Head of Security Engineering
Carbonite Health
